---
title: "Cache and speed"
description: "Where rendered animations are stored, when they are rendered again, and how to keep a deck fast."
---

This guide covers the render cache of `Manim` and `FlowAnimation` and the
settings that keep a deck quick to open.

## Where the cache lives

The first time a cell with an animation runs, Manim renders it, which takes
from one to a few seconds. banners stores the result in

```
~/.cache/banners/manim/
```

and later runs read it from there at once, also after restarting marimo.

## When an animation is rendered again

The cache key includes everything that changes the picture:

- the source code of the scene (for a scene defined in a notebook cell, its
  compiled code), so editing the scene renders it again;
- `quality`, `format` and `interactive`;
- for `FlowAnimation`, the nodes, the edges and the direction;
- the palette of the slide, so the same scene on a slide with another palette
  is a different render.

Code outside the scene that the scene reads at run time, such as a global
variable or a data file, is not part of the key. After changing it, clear the
cache.

## Clear the cache

Deleting the folder is safe; animations are rendered again when needed:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.cache/banners/manim
```

## Keep a deck fast

- **Work in `quality="low"`** and switch to `"medium"` or `"high"` for the
  final version only.
- **Prefer `interactive=True` or `format="mp4"` to long GIFs.** A GIF stores
  every frame as an image: a few seconds at high quality can weigh tens of
  megabytes and exceed marimo's output limit, which then shows "Your output
  is too large" instead of the animation. MP4 is a fraction of that size.
- **Render once before the talk**, so every animation comes from the cache
  during the presentation.
